# dsh-relaunch
**English** | 中文
Restart DeepSeek Harness from its own sidebar.

🎯 The app has no restart command. This adds one — and unlike editing the
application's own files, it
**survives application updates**.

> **Windows only.** The relaunch is implemented with Windows facilities
> (`wscript.exe` for a windo

wless launch, `taskkill` to terminate). On macOS and
> Linux the rail entry still appears, but press

ing it fails cleanly rather than
> doing something unexpected.
## Why

DeepSeek Harness ships no UI for restarting itself. The top bar has an
*Applications* menu, and a re

start item exists in the source — but it sits
behind a `development` flag that production builds nev

er satisfy, so it is not
reachable.

The obvious workaround is to patch the application's `app.asar`. That works
until the first update:

the updater replaces the archive wholesale, your patch
disappears, and the button is gone again. Edi

ting another program's installed
files is also the kind of thing you have to redo forever.

So this does it from the outside. A plugin lives in your DSH profile, which
updates do not touch. It

adds a rail entry to the sidebar; pressing the button
in the panel behind it closes Harness and sta

entry to the sidebar; pressing the button
in the panel behind it closes Harness and starts it again.
## Features

| ⚡ One click | A rail entry beside the shipped panels |
| 🚫 No console flash | The worker is launch

ed windowless, so nothing blinks on screen |
| 🚫 No confirmation dialog | Restart asks nothing; the

panel's button *is* the confirmation |
| 🔁 Survives updates | Installed as a profile plugin, not car

ved into the app |
| 🔒 Explicit | The restart never fires on its own — it needs the button |
| 🌐 Loc
alized | English and Chinese, following the app's language setting |
## What it looks like
The rail entry sits with the shipped panels:
Selecting it opens the panel, whose single button performs the restart:
Both images are captures of the running application, not mock-ups.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then add it to your profile's `package.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The bundle ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the plugin row
process-wide. **A profile

restart is required** — the loader reads its
composition at startup, and the sidebar does not gain t
he entry until then.
## Use
Click the circular-arrow icon in the left rail. The panel has one button.
Pressing it:

1. Sends a request to the plugin's own Host route.
2. Waits a moment so the response can reach the b

rowser first.
3. Terminates the running Harness processes.
4. Starts the application again, verifies
it stayed up, and records each step.

**Everything running is interrupted.** That is what a restart is — DSH
checkpoints sessions as it go

es, so your conversation history survives, but a
task executing at that moment does not.
## How it works

The restart cannot be done from inside the plugin, because the plugin *runs
inside the process being

restarted*. Leaving it to an in-process call would mean
the process kills itself mid-response, and

any child it started would die with
it. So the work goes to a detached worker:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Two details are load-bearing:

- **The launcher is `wscript.exe`, not `powershell.exe`.** PowerShell is a
*console*-subsystem progr

am: starting it allocates a console window that
flashes on screen, and the WMI route used to detach

it cannot ask for
`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. The Harness executable is a *GUI*-subsystem binary, so
running

it in Node mode produces no window at all.
- **The worker strips `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` before rest

arting the app.** That
variable is what makes the worker run as Node instead of as the desktop app.

It is process-scoped, so it is inherited — and an Electron binary that inherits
it starts as a bare

Node runtime with no application logic and exits within a
second, leaving *nothing* running. `test/h

o application logic and exits within a
second, leaving *nothing* running. `test/host.mjs` pins this.
## Requirements

- **Windows.**
- DSH desktop `>= 0.1.7-rc.2` (`engines.dsh`).

The plugin declares **no `@deepseek-ai/*` peer dependency** and imports none of
their values. That i

s deliberate: at startup DSH runs a compatibility check over
every profile bundle, and if even one p

eer range fails to cover the running
version, the whole bundle is skipped — `cordis.patch.yml` never

takes effect and
it looks like "installed but nothing happens". With no peer range to check, that
f
ailure cannot occur here.
## Configuration
None. The plugin has no options; the route and the delay are fixed.
## Known limitations

- **Windows only**, as noted above. The rail entry appears elsewhere but the
restart fails there.
-

**Running tasks are interrupted.** Not a bug, but worth repeating.
- **The plugin needs a profile re

start to appear.** Installing it while Harness
runs links the package, but the sidebar picks up the

entry only after the app
restarts.
- **Only one restart should be in flight at a time.** The button

disables itself
while a restart is running, but nothing prevents a second window from pressing
it to

sables itself
while a restart is running, but nothing prevents a second window from pressing
it too.

## Tests

No DSH host and no dependencies are needed — the suites import only Node
builtins. `host.mjs` covers

the environment leak described above, which is the
one bug in this project that produced a *worse*

outcome than having no plugin at
all.
